regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality test is harder to pass. IIP overall at 6.7% — down from 8.8% — while capital goods surge 16.1% and core sector slows to 5.4% creates a split verdict: investment-led growth is accelerating even as the broader industrial base moderates. The inversion worth noting: PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is being carried by services at 54.5 while manufacturing slips to 52.8 — a services-heavy expansion that flatters the headline but leaves the employment-intensive manufacturing base underperforming.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is not the number that should concern the desk — fuel at 22.93% (95th percentile, up from 20.05%) is. Core CPI at 3.9% sits at only the 28th percentile, which looks benign until you trace the transmission: fuel feeds into transport costs, which feed into food distribution margins, which feed into CFPI — already at 5.52% and rising. RBI's own inflation forecast just jumped 50bps to 5.1%; the gap between that forecast and the current repo rate of 5.25% leaves a real rate of 15bps — insufficient to anchor expectations when WPI is running at 9.92%.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line. CD ratio at 81.4% has eased 110bps from last month but remains at the 75th percentile; the last time it sustained here was FY14, and within 18 months the system required emergency macro-prudential intervention. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding channels are being tapped to bridge what retail deposits cannot — a setup that historically precedes risk-weight tightening, not rate cuts.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% leaves the real policy rate at 15bps — a number that does no work on either inflation expectations or currency defence. INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) is the market's verdict on that arithmetic. The incentive structure is perverse: holding rates steady while forecasting above-target inflation signals that the RBI is prioritising growth support, but with fuel at a decade-high and the rupee under pressure, the cost of that choice is being paid in imported inflation with a two-quarter lag.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up from 75.6%, highest in 18 months — crossing the 75% threshold that historically triggers private capex commitments is the most structurally significant data point this week. IIP capital goods at 16.1% confirms the investment cycle is not a budget artefact; industry credit surging 20% YoY (from 6.5% prior) and services credit at 22.9% (from 10.2%) show that both demand and financing are present. The risk to invert: if the CD ratio forces a deposit rate war that pushes lending rates up 50-75bps, the IRR on new capex projects gets squeezed precisely when the cycle is trying to accelerate.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a 71st-percentile print — strong, but the YTD at only the 14th percentile suggests the monthly beat is partly seasonal and partly advance filing timing, not a clean demand signal. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheelers at 19.7% are the more reliable proxies: two-wheeler strength signals rural and semi-urban recovery (the informal economy's pulse), while PV at 16% confirms urban discretionary is intact. Credit card growth at 2.3% YoY — down from 5.6% and at the 26th percentile — is the quiet contradiction: urban consumers are buying cars but not revolving credit, which either signals financial discipline or early-stage demand fatigue in the mass-affluent segment.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure as smaller lenders chase growth.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force either asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 to ease deposit pressure, not inflation. Position for 50bps easing by June.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically precedes either RBI rate cuts or NBFC stress. Last time we saw this divergence (2022), smaller lenders faced funding crunches within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks 77% — Capex Cycle Firm","data_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up from 75.6% prior month), highest in 18 months. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% but still positive). Industrial credit (industry segment) surging 20% YoY, services credit at 22.9% YoY — both multi-year highs.","implication":"Capex cycle is self-reinforcing. Avoid defensive plays — cyclicals will outperform. Hedge with long-duration bonds; capex-driven growth will keep rates higher for longer.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77% has historically preceded 18-24 months of sustained capex. Last similar reading (2021) led to 3 years of strong capex growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Signals Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (up from ₹31,961 Cr prior month, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (up from ₹18.21 Tr, rising 2 consecutive months). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (up from 99.06 Cr). Critically: SIP AUM growing 2.3% MoM while accounts growing only 1.1% MoM — average ticket size rising sharply, indicating affluent retail entering, not mass-market SIP adoption.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Affluent money entering via SIPs suggests confidence but also signals we're in the upper half of the cycle. Rotate from small-cap to large-cap quality. Overweight dividend-paying large-caps and PSU banks. Reduce exposure to speculative small-caps. DII flows (₹58,502 Cr, 100th percentile) are masking FII weakness — watch for reversal.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile; SIP accounts at 82nd percentile. When AUM growth outpaces account growth by >100bps, it has historically preceded 6-month consolidation in small-caps.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile — CAD Risk Rising","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile). Brent crude at $99.35/bbl (70th percentile, stable). WTI at $95.89/bbl (80th percentile). India's oil import bill rising sharply; fuel inflation feeding into core inflation (CPI core at 3.9%, 28th percentile but rising).","implication":"Current Account Deficit will widen if oil stays >$95/bbl. RBI will resist rate cuts despite deposit pressure — inflation remains the constraint. Overweight energy stocks and refiners (they benefit from high crude). Monitor for RBI FX intervention.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time (2022), it preceded 8 months of RBI hawkishness and INR weakness to 82.5 levels.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Threatens Carry Trade Unwind","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile, strong-negative signal). US 10Y Treasury at 4.94% (down from 5.01%, 89th percentile, strong-negative signal). Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up from 2.0%, 59th percentile). DXY at 100.27 (flat, 51st percentile). US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile, strong-positive).","implication":"BOJ tightening is the wild card. Watch for BOJ guidance in next 2 weeks — a hawkish hold could trigger 5-10% EM correction.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile is a 10-year high for Japanese rates. Last time rates rose this fast (2023), it preceded 3 months of EM volatility and INR weakness.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens to 96.15 — RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.86, 91st percentile, strong-negative signal). Recent trend: 95.24→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24→96.15 (up 3 of last 5 observations, volatile). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (up from ₹20,200 Cr, 83rd percentile, mild-positive). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, strong-positive). Domestic flows masking FII weakness.","implication":"INR weakness is structural — oil imports, rate differentials (US 10Y at 4.94% vs India's implicit real rate), and BOJ carry unwind. RBI will intervene to defend 96.0 but cannot hold indefinitely without rate cuts. Expect INR to test 96.5 in next 4 weeks. Overweight INR hedges for exporters. Importers should lock in forward rates now. FII flows are fragile — any EM shock will reverse them. DII is the only bid; watch for retail fatigue.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness is a 10-year extreme. Last time INR weakened this sharply (2022), it preceded 6 months of RBI rate hikes and 8% further depreciation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Rising While Vacancy Compresses — GCC Thesis Confirmed","data_text":"Office absorption at 48 Mn sqft (55th percentile, neutral). Office vacancy at 13.9% (down from 17.2%, 38th percentile, improving). Rent in Mumbai at ₹171/sqft (up from ₹168, 68th percentile, mild-positive). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹107/sqft (up from ₹100.6, 60th percentile, neutral). Nifty IT flat at 23,346 (75th percentile, neutral). Bank Nifty at 56,359 (93rd percentile, mild-positive). Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (down from 11.6%, 35th percentile, mild-positive).","implication":"Office rents are rising despite Nifty IT being flat — this decouples commercial real estate from the IT services proxy. Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and non-IT corporates are the real demand drivers, not traditional IT services. This means: (1) Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) — they're capturing GCC demand, not IT services demand. (2) Nifty IT weakness is a red herring; office absorption will remain strong. (3) Retail mall vacancy compression suggests discretionary spending is resilient. (4) Avoid shorting IT services on the assumption that office demand will collapse — the demand base has shifted.","pct_10y":60,"pct_note":"Office rents at 60th percentile while IT indices are flat is a 10-year divergence. Historically, office rents and IT stock performance moved together; this decoupling signals a structural shift in tenant composition from IT services to GCCs and financial services.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with capacity utilisation at 77.4% — an 18-month high — is the strongest combination India has printed since the post-COVID capex reboot, but the composition demands scrutiny. IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% from 8.8% even as capital goods surged 16.1%, which means the investment cycle is real but the broader industrial base is not yet participating. Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY confirm rural demand is recovering — the informal economy's most reliable barometer — while credit card growth at 2.3% (26th percentile) suggests urban mass-market spending is more measured than the GST headline implies. The growth story is genuine; it is also narrower than the 7.8% print suggests.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US GDP at 1.5% SAAR — down from 2.1% — while US PMI composite hits 56.0 (84th percentile) is the central contradiction in global macro: activity surveys are pricing a soft landing that the hard GDP data is already questioning. BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile) is the structural shift that matters most for EM carry — every 25bps of Japanese normalisation tightens global dollar liquidity by more than an equivalent Fed move, because it unwinds a decade of yen-funded positioning. China's composite PMI at 49.5 with GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) removes the one engine that could have offset US softness — copper at $6.71/lb (80th percentile) is holding, but iron ore's volatility signals the commodity complex is reading China's trajectory with more scepticism than equity markets are.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile print, rising for two consecutive months — is absorbing every rupee of FII ambivalence, but the composition of that domestic flow is shifting in a way that matters. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 trillion is growing at 2.3% MoM while SIP accounts grow only 1.1% MoM — average ticket size is rising sharply, which means affluent retail is entering, not mass-market adoption broadening. That is a qualitatively different liquidity source: stickier in normal times, but more correlated with equity market levels and more likely to pause if Nifty corrects 8-10%. US 10Y at 4.94% — easing from 5.01% but still at the 89th percentile — keeps the opportunity cost of EM equity elevated for foreign allocators, and INR at 96.15 adds a currency drag that FII return calculations cannot ignore.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 56,359 (93rd percentile) is pricing a credit cycle that the deposit data does not yet support — with CD ratio at 81.4% and deposit growth at 10.8%, any macro-prudential tightening on risk weights would compress NIMs and trigger earnings downgrades that passive index flows would amplify on the way down. Office real estate is the cleaner story: vacancy compressing to 13.9% from 17.2% with Bengaluru rents up 6.4% to ₹107/sqft confirms the GCC absorption thesis, yet Embassy, Mindspace, and Brookfield REITs are all trading well below prior levels — the physical market and the listed vehicle are pricing the same asset differently, and that gap historically closes upward. Gold at ₹13,632/gram (100th percentile, rising 4 of 5 sessions) is the hedge that domestic capital is quietly building — not against global risk, but against a rupee that a 15bps real rate cannot defend.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact. First: fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) with Brent at $99.35 — every $5 move toward $105 adds roughly ₹75,000 crore to the annual import bill, widens CAD by 20bps, and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag that the RBI's 5.1% forecast may not fully capture. Second: BOJ at 1.0% with US 10Y still at the 89th percentile creates the conditions for a carry-trade unwind that would hit INR, EM bonds, and India's ₹58,502 crore DII-supported equity market simultaneously — the domestic bid is large but not infinite. Third: the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% sets up a regulatory response risk — the RBI has used risk-weight increases twice in the last cycle to cool unsecured lending, and the incentive to act again is rising. Watch Friday's RBI weekly credit-deposit data for any further widening of the 630bps gap — that is the single number that determines whether the base case holds or the bear scenario begins.

"}
